learnings: Citation parsing requires format-specific regex - IEEE most structured, Nature most compact, inline least information
Confidence scoring key to prioritizing verification work - DOI presence boosts confidence by 30%
Claim detection needs multi-stage approach: patterns first (high precision), then heuristics (broader coverage)
LSS drift thresholds aligned with provenance confidence levels: 5% warning, 15% alert, 30% critical
OWASP A03 (Injection) critical for parsers - validate all input text, reject oversized payloads
Hedging language inversely correlates with claim certainty - count hedges to adjust confidence
Severity-certainty consistency checking catches researcher over/under-confidence
Streaming detection enables real-time claim flagging during document authoring

patterns: Parser architecture: Format detection → Extraction → Normalization → Validation - reusable across citation/claim/parameter parsing
Fail-loudly pattern: Input validation with descriptive errors, no silent fallbacks that hide bugs
Batch + streaming pattern: Provide both bulk processing and incremental APIs for different use cases
Statistics-first: Every extraction/detection returns stats object for monitoring and optimization
Confidence scoring: Combine multiple signals (DOI, venue, completeness) into 0-1 score for prioritization
insights: Research integrity requires infrastructure, not vigilance - automated detection catches what humans miss
Citation extraction confidence distribution follows power law - most are 0.4-0.6, few are >0.9
Claim detection recall vs precision tradeoff: lower threshold finds more claims, higher threshold reduces false positives
LSS effective for drift detection when cited values known - integration with citation-verifier creates feedback loop
Platform engineering is about building systems that enforce rigor, not relying on discipline
Security is not optional - OWASP controls must be integrated from day 1, not bolted on
Nested Learning provides multi-timescale consolidation that prevents temporary states from becoming permanent facts
LSS (Local Surprise Signal) is the key to automated monitoring - high surprise = something needs attention
Type-driven development prevents entire classes of bugs - TypeScript strictness pays dividends in research code
